title: Monotonicity of majority noise stability
statement: Let $\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0\leq\rho\leq1$, and let $m\in\mathbb N$. For a Boolean function $f$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, define its noise stability by $\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(f)=\langle f,T_{\rho}f\rangle$, where $T_{\rho}f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x)$ and the inner product and Fourier coefficients use the uniform measure. Then the majority functions on the two respective odd-dimensional cubes satisfy $\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(M_{m+1})\leq\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(M_m)$.
replaced:
Let $m\in\mathbb N$ and $\rho\in[0,1]$, and for each $q\in\mathbb N$ define
$M_q:\{\pm1\}^{2q+1}\to\mathbb R$ to equal $1$ when more than $q$ coordinates equal $1$,
and $-1$ otherwise.
For any $d\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{\pm1\}^d\to\mathbb R$, define
$\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)=\mathbb E[f(X)f(Y)]$, where $X$ is uniform on
$\{\pm1\}^d$ and, independently in each coordinate, $Y_i=-X_i$ with probability
$(1-\rho)/2$ and $Y_i=X_i$ otherwise; then
\[
 \operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_{m+1})\le\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(M_m).
\]
